Subject: An Update on Your Brewlog Pre-Order

Here's the honest news: our Bluetooth certification hit an unexpected delay, so shipping now starts on March 17 instead of March 3. We know you want to start brewing, and we're sorry for the wait.

1,200 repositories.

When we launched Patchwork CI, we made a promise: always free for open source. People told us we were crazy. "How will you make money?" they asked.

Today we run on 1,200 repositories. About 900 of them are open source.

Here's what surprised me. Across all those repos, 1 in 7 CI failures turned out to be a flaky test. Countless hours of your time, burned on red builds that weren't real failures.

Open source didn't just give us users. It gave us data, feedback, and a community. Our most-requested feature, GitLab support, came straight from OSS maintainers. We shipped it on November 12.

Giving back isn't charity. It's strategy.

#OpenSource #DevOps #CI #DeveloperExperience #BuildInPublic

1,000 families.

14 months ago, Pebble Pantry was just an idea I scribbled down during maternity leave. I was sleep-deprived, overwhelmed, and staring at an empty fridge at 7pm.

Today, 1,000 families pay €4.99 a month to make dinner time just a little bit easier.

And here's the most beautiful part: we didn't get here through fancy ad campaigns or growth hacks. Most of our families found us through school WhatsApp groups, parents recommending us to other parents.

That's not just growth. That's trust.

To every mum and dad who shared us in a group chat: thank you. You built this with us.

To every founder building on a shoestring: keep going. Your community is your superpower.

#Startups #Portugal #Parenting #FemaleFounders #Gratitude

Losing our first big customer was the best thing that ever happened to Ledgerline.

Let me explain. 5 months in, they walked away, and it stung. A lot.

But failure isn't the opposite of success. It's part of it.

The reason they left: they had heavily customized their NetSuite instance, and we only supported standard fields. We weren't meeting them where they were.

So we did what great teams do. We listened, we learned, and we built.

We spent 6 weeks adding support for custom fields. It wasn't just a feature. It was a fundamental shift in how we think about our customers.

Today, we serve 38 customers, and 11 of them rely on custom fields.

The lesson is that your biggest setback can become your biggest breakthrough.

Lean into the hard feedback. Your customers are telling you what to build, and you just have to listen.

What's a loss that shaped your company?

#Startups #SaaS #Leadership #CustomerSuccess #Growth

We built an app we were proud of. Almost nobody used it.

When we launched Rotaship, we assumed restaurant staff would love our sleek mobile app. Then the numbers came in: only 12% of staff even opened it in the first month.

That stung. We weren't solving the real problem. We were adding another one.

Restaurant teams don't want another app. They live on WhatsApp.

So in 2025, we made the call and moved everything into WhatsApp.

It worked. 140 outlets now use it, and the median reply time to shift messages is under 20 minutes.

If you're building for busy people, meet them where they already are. Don't wait for them to come to you.

Sometimes the best product decision is letting go of the thing you love.

#ProductManagement #Indonesia #StartupLessons #UserExperience

After 11 years in a clinic, I walked away. Here's why.

I've always loved being a vet. But something kept breaking my heart.

Day after day, I'd see anxious pets so terrified that we had to sedate them just to examine them.

I knew there had to be a better way.

So in 2023, I took the leap and founded Doorstep Vet.

The idea was simple yet powerful: bring compassionate, high-quality care to pets in the one place they feel safest, their own home.

Today, our incredible team of 4 vets does around 30 home visits a week. And every single one is a reminder of why we do this.

Calmer pets. Happier owners. Better medicine.

Sometimes the bravest thing you can do is follow your heart.

#Veterinary #PetCare #Melbourne #Entrepreneurship #FollowYourPassion

We raised our prices by 50%. Here's what happened.

In September, we made one of the scariest calls in Tabwise's history: our price went from $8 to $12 per user per month.

Why? Our support costs per customer had doubled since launch. So we had a choice. Cut quality, or charge what we're actually worth.

We chose value.

But we weren't about to leave loyal customers holding the bill. Every existing customer kept their $8 price for 12 months.

The result? Two of 140 customers churned in the next 2 months.

Two.

Here's the lesson: customers don't pay for software. They pay for outcomes. Price accordingly.

Founders, when did you last raise your prices?

#SaaS #Pricing #StartupLessons #Growth #B2B

Hardware is hard, so here is our story.

Our first production run at Shelfwise didn't go as planned. We shipped 400 labels with a faulty battery contact.

As a young hardware startup, it would have been easy to cut corners. But that's not who we are.

We decided to recall and replace every one of those 400 labels at our own cost. It set us back about $7,000. Painful? Absolutely. Worth it? 100%.

Because trust is everything.

We didn't stop there. We introduced a 100% contact test at the factory. Since then, we've had zero contact failures across 6,000 labels.

Mistakes don't define you. How you respond to them does.

To all the hardware founders out there: own your mistakes, fix them fast, and build systems so they never happen again.

#Hardware #Startups #Manufacturing #Leadership #Integrity

Why we stopped billing by the hour, and never looked back.

When we started Fernway Studio, we did what every agency does: we charged hourly. 4 of our first 6 projects went over budget. Clients were frustrated. So were we. Trust was eroding.

So in 2024, we made a bold decision. We switched to a fixed price: KES 450,000 per Shopify store. Period. It changed everything.

Clients know exactly what they're paying. We're incentivized to work smarter, not longer. Relationships are built on trust, not timesheets.

Since then, we've launched 31 stores. Only 2 went over our 6-week timeline.

Pricing isn't just a number. It's a promise.

Founders, how do you price your services? Tell me in the comments.

#Entrepreneurship #Africa #Shopify #AgencyLife #Pricing

3 days. That's how long one spindle failure shut down our line.

Years ago, I was a maintenance engineer at an auto-parts plant in Pune. One day, a spindle failed, and an entire production line sat dead for 3 long days.

Here's the part that still haunts me: the warning signs were there. 2 weeks earlier, vibration readings had shown the problem clearly. Nobody was watching.

That moment changed everything. In 2022, I founded Ferrous so no manufacturer has to live through that kind of preventable downtime again.

Today, our sensors sit on 410 machines across 17 plants.

Every reading tells a story. Every alert is a breakdown that didn't happen. Every plant brings Indian manufacturing one step closer to what it should be.

Data only matters if someone is listening.

#Manufacturing #Industry40 #PredictiveMaintenance #MakeInIndia #StartupStory

Why we walked away from the 25% recruiting fee.

So in January, we made a bold move: a flat $18,000 per hire. No percentages, no games.

The result is that we've placed 26 senior Rust engineers this year, and our relationships with clients have never been stronger.

It's time for the recruiting industry to evolve. Founders deserve better.

Would you work with a flat-fee recruiter? Let me know.

#Recruiting #Startups #RustLang #Hiring #FutureOfWork

At Linguo Labs, our team of 14 spans Estonia, Latvia, Finland, and Sweden. We've never been more connected.
